notes: This ledger tracks entries that have been manually checked against their cited source or a stronger replacement source.
Status values: verified, verified_with_note, corrected, source_corrected, source_improved.

checks.notes: HSE confirms the Dec. 11, 2005 Buncefield explosions, major fire, over 40 injuries and no fatalities. The existing source is an overview page with links to detailed reports; the stuck gauge/IHLS mechanism should be checked against the linked investigation report in a later deep pass.

The previous URL pointed to a 2018 Waterloo RAIB report, not the 1988 Clapham Junction crash. Replaced it with the Hidden Report entry at The Railways Archive and changed the source label accordingly.
NTSB source confirms the Dec. 15, 1967 U.S. 35 bridge collapse, 46 deaths and investigation framing. ASCE also supports the single-cracked-eyebar and redundancy lesson.
NPS source confirms Orville Wright piloted the Dec. 17, 1903 first flight for 12 seconds and 120 feet. The three-axis-control interpretation is sound but not fully supported by this NPS page alone.
CSB confirms the Dec. 19, 2007 T2 Laboratories explosion, four deaths, hospitalizations/injuries, reactive incident classification, and cooling-system/runaway-reaction cause.
DOE confirms that on Dec. 20, 1951 EBR-I became the first power plant to produce usable electricity through atomic fission, initially powering four 200-watt lightbulbs.
Replaced the broad EPA coal-ash rule page with EPA response page specific to Kingston. It confirms Dec. 22, 2008, dike failure, about 5.4 million cubic yards released and about 300 acres affected.

Harvard Countway source supports the Dec. 23, 1954 successful transplant between Ronald and Richard Herrick. The page intermittently blocks direct fetch, but the indexed source metadata matches the entry.
NASA confirms Webb launched Dec. 25, 2021 on Ariane 5, used a folded/stowed launch configuration, and deployed on the journey toward L2.
FAA confirms the Dec. 29, 1972 crash, nose-gear indication distraction, unnoticed descent, 112 deaths, and the crew resource management lesson.

Stanford Medicine confirms that Norman Shumway performed the first U.S. adult heart transplant on Jan. 6, 1968, with Mike Kasperak as the recipient, and supports the surgical preparation, preservation and rejection-control framing.

The AAIB page is the official report landing page for the Jan. 8, 1989 Boeing 737-400 accident. A FAA lessons-learned page directly exposes the left-engine fan-blade failure, right-engine shutdown and cockpit-cue chain, so the source is retained with supporting evidence noted.
Apple confirms the Jan. 9, 2007 introduction and the combined phone, widescreen iPod, internet communicator and multi-touch software-interface claims.
Transport for London confirms the Jan. 10, 1863 first Metropolitan Railway journey between Paddington and Farringdon and describes it as the world's first underground railway.

CDC confirms the Jan. 13, 1993 physician report to Washington health officials, the E. coli O157:H7 illness cluster, and linkage to hamburgers from a restaurant chain with undercooked ground beef as the control issue.

Replaced the thinner NPS event page with a City of Boston source. It confirms Jan. 15, 1919, the 50-foot tank rupture, 2.3 million gallons released, 21 deaths, 150 injuries, elevated-rail damage, and structural concerns about wall thickness and cracking.

Updated the stale TWI URL to the live article. The Welding Institute confirms the Jan. 16, 1943 dockside fracture, that Schenectady broke in two amidships, and the brittle-fracture/material-toughness lesson.

The cited NHHC page intermittently times out in the crawler, but indexed NHHC content confirms that Nautilus was the world's first nuclear-powered submarine and on Jan. 17, 1955 was underway on nuclear power. The Navy's Nuclear Navy page also supports the same date and milestone.

NIST supports the Jan. 18, 1978 Hartford Civic Arena roof collapse after snow and freezing rain and frames it within structural load/reliability lessons. The detailed modelling/design-assumption language is supported by engineering secondary sources and should get a deeper primary-source pass later.

University of Toronto Libraries confirms Leonard Thompson first received Banting and Best's extract on Jan. 11, 1922, then Collip's purified extract on Jan. 23; the second test was dramatically successful and lowered blood sugar to normal in one day.

Computer History Museum confirms the Jan. 24, 1984 Macintosh launch, graphical user interface, mouse-driven point-and-click interaction, compact all-in-one design context and mass-market usability framing.

Science Museum Group confirms Baird repeated his light-and-shade television experiments for Royal Institution members on Jan. 26, 1926 after earlier experiments with Stooky Bill, supporting the working-television demonstration framing.

NASA confirms the Jan. 27, 1967 launch-pad test fire and deaths of Grissom, White and Chaffee, and links to the Apollo 204 Review Board report. The oxygen, combustible-materials and hatch details are supported by the linked review materials rather than fully exposed on the overview page.

Rogers Commission chapter confirms the cold launch context, aft field-joint smoke, incomplete sealing action, O-ring erosion by hot propellant gases, flame plume from the right solid rocket booster and rapid vehicle breakup around 73 seconds.

Mercedes-Benz Group confirms Carl Benz applied on Jan. 29, 1886 for patent number 37435 for a vehicle powered by a gas engine and describes the engine/chassis integration of the three-wheeled Patent Motor Car.
NASA confirms Explorer 1 launched Jan. 31, 1958 as the first U.S. satellite and carried James Van Allen's cosmic-ray instrument package, supporting the discovery-oriented prototype lesson.

NASA confirms Columbia suffered catastrophic failure during re-entry on Feb. 1, 2003 due to a breach from falling external-tank foam striking the reinforced carbon-carbon panels on the underside of the left wing.

NTSB confirms the Feb. 3, 2023 East Palestine derailment, failed and overheated wheel bearing, hazardous-material release and fire, and failure of wayside monitoring systems to diagnose the hot bearing in time.
CSB confirms the Feb. 7, 2008 Imperial Sugar explosion and fire at Port Wentworth, 14 deaths, 38 injuries and massive combustible sugar-dust accumulations throughout the packaging building.

Boeing page confirms the first 747 took off on Feb. 9, 1969 and notes Everett factory construction began in 1966 and remains the world's largest building by volume. Source is retained, though a dedicated Boeing history page would be cleaner if one becomes available.

Penn CIS confirms ENIAC was unveiled at the University of Pennsylvania on Feb. 15 and was all-electronic and programmable. Keep note that some institutional histories distinguish a Feb. 14 public/press announcement from the Feb. 15 formal dedication/presentation.

NASA confirms John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth on Feb. 20, 1962, completed three orbits, flew 4 hours 55 minutes 23 seconds, and that Project Mercury aimed to place a piloted spacecraft in orbit, observe human performance, and recover both safely.

Replaced obsolete raib.gov.uk URL with current GOV.UK RAIB report page. RAIB confirms the Feb. 23, 2007 Virgin West Coast derailment at 2B points near Grayrigg/Lambrigg and the failures of stretcher bars, lock stretcher bar and fastenings, plus inspection and maintenance factors.

NTSB confirms the Feb. 24, 1989 United 811 explosive decompression after the forward lower-lobe cargo door separated during climb from Honolulu, the successful emergency return, and nine passengers lost at sea.

GAO full report confirms the Feb. 25, 1991 Dhahran Patriot failure, continuous operation for over 100 hours, inaccurate time calculation, range-gate shift and failure to track/intercept the incoming Scud.

RAF Museum confirms the Feb. 26, 1935 practical demonstration proposed by R.A. Watson-Watt: Daventry transmitter signals reflected from a Handley Page Heyford and detected by Slough Radio Research Station staff at Weedon.
Raspberry Pi confirms the first units went on sale on Feb. 29, 2012 via element14 and RS Components, with over 100,000 orders on the first day and demand far beyond the original expectations.

Airbus confirms Concorde 001 first flew from Toulouse at 3:38pm on Mar. 2, 1969, that the maiden flight lasted 29 minutes, and that the Franco-British programme had a formal 50:50 research and assembly cost share.

MAIB/GOV.UK page confirms the Mar. 6, 1987 flooding and capsize of the ro-ro ferry with loss of 193 lives and links the formal investigation report. The visible page summary does not spell out bow-door status, so that detail is treated as supported by the linked formal report rather than the landing-page text alone.

Library of Congress search snippets/about collection confirm Bell's March 10, 1876 experimental notebook pages describe the first successful telephone experiment and the words to Watson. Original cited LOC bulletin intermittently blocks fetches, so this ledger entry points to the more stable LOC collection page.

DOE Idaho FOIA reading room lists the official SL-1 accident reports for the Jan. 3, 1961 Stationary Low-Power Reactor No. 1 accident. DOE oral-history footnotes and INL history pages support that crew were reconnecting control rods for restart, a steam explosion occurred, and all three crew members died; the detailed rapid power-excursion analysis is in the linked official reports.

EBRD confirms the Nov. 29, 2016 milestone: the New Safe Confinement was moved 327 metres into final position over Chornobyl Unit 4, enclosing the 1986 makeshift shelter. The page also confirms the 36,000-tonne movable land-based arch and its 100-year safety/dismantling purpose.

IAEA confirms the 11 March 2011 earthquake and tsunami, Fukushima Daiichi accident, INES Level 7 classification, and later safety-improvement/action-plan work. The current entry's shared-hazard lesson is editorial but consistent with the reported loss of multiple safety elements after the external event.

Replaced the broad Bureau of Reclamation case-history PDF with the ASDSO Dam Failures case study, which directly supports the March 12-13, 1928 breach, concrete gravity dam context, abutment/foundation geology, uplift/sliding concerns, and foundation-failure lesson.

NEJM article/search metadata supports six healthy volunteers, TGN1412 administration and severe cytokine-release reactions. JCI directly supports that ten minutes was too short an interval between dosing and that longer observation could have spared the other five volunteers. Current NEJM page is retained as the source but is crawler-hostile.

National Archives confirms Whitney's cotton gin patent date of 3/14/1794, its seed-from-fiber function, short-staple cotton improvement, production impact, and the linked social consequence around expansion of slavery.

NTSB confirms the 3/15/2018 FIU pedestrian bridge collapse, load-and-capacity calculation errors, inadequate peer review, observed cracking, and failure to close the road as the cracking became unacceptable.

NASA confirms Goddard's first liquid-fueled rocket launch on March 16, 1926 in Auburn, Massachusetts, using gasoline and liquid oxygen, and gives the short flight performance that supports the modest-experiment lesson.

MIT Lemelson confirms Volta revealed the Voltaic Pile on March 20, 1800, using alternating silver and zinc with brine-soaked cloth, and that it provided continuous current as the world's first battery.

CSB confirms the March 23, 2005 Texas City refinery explosion, 15 deaths, 180 injuries, restart of the hydrocarbon isomerization unit, tower flooding/overpressure, and organizational/process-safety management deficiencies.

NTSB confirms the March 24, 1989 Exxon Valdez grounding on Bligh Reef, ice-avoidance course correction, eight ruptured cargo tanks, large crude-oil spill, third-mate bridge control and fatigue/manning concerns.

Replaced a crawler-hostile DOL history URL with OSHA's Triangle account. OSHA confirms the March 25 fire at the Triangle Waist Company factory, 146 deaths, one collapsed fire escape, locked/wrong-way doors, trapped workers, poor fire protection and the workplace-safety reform legacy.

FAA confirms the Mar. 27, 1977 Tenerife collision between KLM 4805 and Pan Am 1736, both Boeing 747s, after KLM initiated takeoff while Pan Am was still taxiing on the runway. It supports the fog, congested/diverted airport, ambiguous radio language, operational pressure and 583-fatality context.

NRC confirms the Mar. 28, 1979 Three Mile Island Unit 2 partial meltdown, equipment malfunctions, design-related problems, worker errors, misleading valve indication, inadequate core-state information and subsequent control-room/human-factors reforms.

The official Eiffel Tower history confirms completion on Mar. 31, 1889 after two years, two months and five days, 18,038 metallic parts, 5,300 workshop designs, 2,500,000 rivets and tenth-of-a-millimetre preparation accuracy.
NASA confirms TIROS 1 launched on Apr. 1, 1960 as the nation's first weather satellite, operated for 78 days and demonstrated monitoring of Earth's cloud cover and weather patterns from space.

CSB confirms the Apr. 2, 2010 Tesoro Anacortes explosion and fire, seven worker deaths, nearly 40-year-old heat exchanger, startup after maintenance shutdown and long-term undetected high-temperature hydrogen attack. The current source URL remains the main CSB investigation page; this evidence URL is a CSB news/video page that exposes the startup wording more directly.

Motorola Solutions confirms that on Apr. 3, 1973 Motorola publicly demonstrated the world's first working prototype portable cellular system and phone, DynaTAC, in New York City, after work on portable two-way and pre-cellular systems.

Crossness Engines Trust confirms the official opening on Apr. 4, 1865 by HRH Albert Edward, Prince of Wales, as part of Bazalgette's southern outfall works, with sewage lifted into a covered reservoir and released on the ebb tide.

Replaced the older MSHA fatality URL, which now fails in fetches, with MSHA's live final-report URL. MSHA/NTIS metadata support the Apr. 5, 2010 Upper Big Branch explosion, 29 deaths, methane ignition/coal-dust explosion framing and failures in ventilation, rock dusting, equipment maintenance and safety management.

NASA History confirms COMSAT's Early Bird launched from Cape Canaveral on Apr. 6, 1965 and states global satellite communications had begun. The same page notes by the end of 1965 Early Bird had provided 150 telephone half-circuits and 80 hours of television service, so the entry's title is launch-centered while operational service matured after launch.

IBM confirms System/360 launched on Apr. 7, 1964 as a unified software-compatible architecture replacing five existing IBM product lines, covering six processor models and 54 peripherals, and pioneering the 8-bit byte.

ESA confirms that Yuri Gagarin became the first human to fly in space on Apr. 12, 1961, completing one orbit in a 108-minute Vostok 1 mission. The entry's description of integrating launch, life support, orbital flight and return is a sound engineering synthesis rather than wording stated directly on the source page.

U.S. Coast Guard history confirms Titanic struck an iceberg late on Apr. 14, sank on Apr. 15, 1912, lost roughly 1,500 people and prompted lifesaving improvements and the International Ice Patrol. The dataset date correctly refers to the sinking; the cited NOAA page is official but was not retrievable by the checker.

NOAA confirms the Apr. 16, 1947 Grandcamp fire and ammonium-nitrate explosion at Texas City, followed about 16 hours later by the explosion of the nearby High Flyer. The source also supports the scale and the danger of treating the smoking cargo as an ordinary shipboard fire.

The U.S. Chemical Safety Board confirms that approximately 30 tons of fertilizer-grade ammonium nitrate exploded after being heated by a fire on Apr. 17, 2013, killing 15 people, injuring more than 260 and damaging nearby homes and schools.

The U.S. Chemical Safety Board confirms the Apr. 20, 2010 Macondo blowout and Deepwater Horizon explosion, 11 deaths and the blowout preventer's failure during emergency well control. The precise negative-pressure-test interpretation is documented in the linked investigation reports rather than fully summarized on the landing page.

NASA confirms Hubble's Apr. 24, 1990 launch, the primary-mirror flaw and the first servicing mission's corrective optics. The history also supports the entry's lesson that planned on-orbit serviceability made recovery possible.

CDC confirms the Apr. 25, 2014 source switch and subsequent pipe corrosion and lead leaching; the EPA Inspector General confirms that inadequate water treatment after the switch exposed residents to lead. The corrosion-control mechanism is supported more explicitly by the EPA report than by the current CDC landing page.

The IAEA confirms that Unit 4 went out of control during a planned low-power test on Apr. 26, 1986, causing an explosion and fire. It also identifies reactor and shutdown-system design, procedural violations and weak safety culture as contributing factors.

Airbus confirms the A380's first flight from Toulouse on Apr. 27, 2005, its unprecedented passenger-aircraft scale and enabling digital and materials innovations. The entry's global logistics and interface-control framing is a reasonable engineering synthesis but is not detailed on this anniversary page.

The NTSB confirms the Apr. 28, 1988 explosive decompression, separation of an approximately 18-foot upper-fuselage section and loss of one flight attendant. It attributes the accident to failures to detect lap-joint disbonding and fatigue damage, with maintenance-program and oversight contributors.

CERN confirms that on Apr. 30, 1993 it released the World Wide Web software into the public domain, relinquishing intellectual-property rights to the source and binary code and allowing anyone to use, duplicate, modify and redistribute it.

The Empire State Building's official history confirms the 102-story building was constructed between Mar. 17, 1930 and May 1, 1931—one year and 45 days—and officially opened on May 1. The cited page does not detail every production-method claim about standardized steelwork, delivery coordination and repetitive floor planning.
LeShuttle confirms the Channel Tunnel was officially opened on May 6, 1994, was excavated simultaneously from Britain and France, and consists of two running tunnels plus a central service tunnel.

The NTSB confirms that Summit Venture struck a support pier on May 9, 1980, dropping about 1,297 feet of bridge into Tampa Bay and killing 35 people. It explicitly identifies the lack of a structural pier-protection system and a motorist-warning system as contributors, supporting both the title and lesson.

The National Park Service confirms that the Central Pacific and Union Pacific lines met at Promontory Summit on May 10, 1869, completing the Transcontinental Railroad, and that a nationwide telegraph message announced the connection.

The NTSB confirms the May 11, 1996 crash and all 110 deaths. It found that a cargo-compartment fire was initiated by improperly carried chemical oxygen generators and identified failures in their preparation, packaging and identification plus ValuJet and FAA oversight.

NASA confirms Skylab launched on May 14, 1973 as the first U.S. space station; launch forces tore away its thermal micrometeoroid shield, lost one solar array and trapped the other. Engineers and astronauts developed repairs that allowed three crews to complete productive missions.

BAE Systems Heritage confirms Britain's first jet aircraft made its 17-minute first flight on May 15, 1941 with a Whittle W.1 engine. It describes the E.28/39 as a technology demonstrator and states that it led directly to the Gloster Meteor.

The UK government's independent review confirms that a gas explosion in an 18th-floor kitchen on May 16, 1968 caused an entire corner of the 22-story Ronan Point tower to collapse, killing four people and injuring 17, and that the event drove structural-code changes.

The Computer History Museum confirms that Robert Metcalfe wrote the original Ethernet memo at Xerox PARC on May 22, 1973, proposing a way to connect computers. Ethernet's broader role as a foundation for local networking and later internet infrastructure is accurate historical context but is only briefly supported by this page.

The cited New York City Municipal Archives collection guide was not readable by the checker, so the opening date and engineering significance were cross-checked against National Park Service documentation and Library of Congress material. The mixed rail, road and pedestrian use describes the bridge's operating system over time, not necessarily every service on opening day.

The FAA confirms the May 25, 1979 accident, separation of the left engine and pylon, severed hydraulic and electrical systems, retraction of the left-wing slats and loss of the cockpit warnings that would have alerted the crew to the developing stall.

The Golden Gate Bridge District confirms Pedestrian Day on May 27, 1937, followed by the opening to vehicle traffic on May 28. Its official history also supports the record-setting main span and the project's ahead-of-schedule, under-budget completion.

The BEA confirms the June 1, 2009 loss, temporary pitot icing, erroneous airspeed indications, subsequent stall and failure to apply an appropriate response. The concise event page does not expose every cockpit-system detail; the autopilot-disconnection sequence is documented in the final investigation report.

The MIT-hosted Leveson and Turner account identifies the first Therac-25 overdose at Kennestone Regional Oncology Center on June 3, 1985 and documents the machine's increased reliance on software without independent hardware interlocks.

ESA confirms the June 4, 1996 loss of Ariane 501 and attributes it to inertial-reference-system software specification and design errors. The official inquiry report provides the detailed conversion-overflow and Ariane 4 software-reuse chain summarized by the entry.

The Bureau of Reclamation confirms the June 5, 1976 catastrophic failure, the observed seepage and unsuccessful efforts to plug it before the breach. The detailed first-filling and internal-erosion mechanism is documented in the linked technical history and reports rather than fully restated on the landing page.

The U.S. Chemical Safety Board confirms the June 13, 2013 explosion, an offline reboiler isolated from its pressure-relief path, heat and pressure accumulation, the resulting BLEVE, two deaths and 167 injuries.

The UK government's response to the inquiry confirms the June 14, 2017 kitchen fire, its escape into the external envelope, rapid spread around the tower and 72 deaths. It also supports the entry's cladding, testing and regulatory-failure framing.

Corrected the orbit count from 49 to 48. ESA confirms the June 16, 1963 launch, nearly three-day mission, flight log and experiments; the UK Space Agency and Science Museum both report 48 Earth orbits.

The University of Manchester confirms that the Baby successfully ran its first program on June 21, 1948 and was the first electronic digital computer able to store both program and data electronically.

The NTSB confirms the June 22, 2009 rear-end collision, nine deaths and the failed track-circuit module that stopped detecting the stationary train and transmitted speed commands to the following train.

NIST's June 2026 technical findings confirm the June 24, 2021 partial collapse and 98 deaths, and identify failures at two garage-column/pool-deck connections followed by load redistribution in a structure with low margins, construction deviations and corrosion. The title's 'without warning' refers to the immediate collapse, not an absence of earlier signs of deterioration.

The Smithsonian confirms that the first supermarket scanner installation entered service at a Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio on June 26, 1974, supporting the date, place and first operational UPC-scan claim.

The FAA confirms the June 30, 1956 collision of a TWA Super Constellation and United DC-7 while operating under visual flight rules, the loss of all 128 people aboard and the accident's role in major air-traffic-control reform.

Sony's corporate history confirms that the first Walkman went on sale July 1, 1979, combined a playback-only portable stereo with lightweight headphones and established a new form of mobile personal listening.

The Science Museum Group identifies Haber's sealed-tube sample as the first liquefied ammonia synthesized on July 2, 1909 and explains how the process enabled synthetic fertilizer production from atmospheric nitrogen.

The Mercedes-Benz Public Archive confirms that Benz designed the engine, chassis and drivetrain as an integrated purpose-built automobile and made the Patent Motor Car's first public road drive in Mannheim on July 3, 1886.

The official Cullen inquiry supports the July 6, 1988 Piper Alpha event and the maintenance, permit-to-work and communication chain summarized by the entry. The HSE landing page is only an index; the detailed mechanism is contained in the scanned inquiry volumes.

The European Commission's Joint Research Centre confirms the July 10, 1976 runaway reactor event at the TCP plant near Seveso, the release of a toxic cloud containing TCDD and the accident's role in creating the European Seveso industrial-safety framework.
